subject: Proposal: Aligning contract runway & phased capacity uplift for Acme Health
summary: Discussion to shift Acme Health renewal to a 24-month co-term with a three-stage capacity ramp, auto-renew language with opt-out windows, and a small introductory credit in year one. Internal alignment on pricing ladder and legal review required. Next step: share updated proposal and get procurement confirmation for signatures.
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Aligning contract runway & phased capacity uplift for Acme Health

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, attached is a clean proposal that moves Acme from a 12-month usage-first contract to a 24-month co-term with a phased capacity uplift. High level:

- Term: 24 months (co-term with the Acme Platform contract)
- Ramp: three stages across the first 12 months (25% -> 50% -> 100% of committed capacity)
- Auto-renew: 12-month auto-renew thereafter with a 60-day opt-out window before renewal
- Credits: a one-time $15k credit applied in Q1 of the new term to offset onboarding and integration costs
- SLO / fallback: we include a temporary burst allowance for the first 90 days and an agreed SLA credit if median p95 latency exceeds targets for two consecutive quarters

Attachments: acme-phased-uplift-proposal-v1.pdf, acme-capacity-map-2026.xlsx (shows expected traffic growth and recommended quantized tiers).

Ask: can you confirm whether Procurement wants the co-term to sync to the Platform contract anniversary or to a fiscal-quarter boundary? That determines the proration approach in section 3.

If that works, we can prepare a DocuSign packet and loop legal for a short redline. Suggested next milestone: procurement confirmation by end of next week so we can lock pricing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales (West)
Redwood Inference

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we pass to Procurement:

1) For the ramp percentages, are the units tokens or vCPU-hours? We assume tokens but want to confirm for our finance team.
2) The 60-day opt-out: does that require a termination fee if executed within the first renewal?
3) For the $15k credit, can that be applied as an invoice credit over two quarters instead of a one-time offset?

I'll loop Procurement (cc'd) and Jason (platform lead) — Jason, any concerns about the burst allowance impacting our internal throttles?

If possible, could you show a proration example for both (a) syncing to our Platform anniversary (Sept 1) and (b) syncing to calendar Q4 boundary? That will help Procurement decide.

Thanks — Olivia
Head of AI Platform
